title: El Cuerpo Y El Descanso
label: ch:es-cuerpo
canDo: I can say where I exercise, report an injury the way a clinic expects to hear it, say I have to rest, and close the story by laughing about it.

payoff.summary: Read the notice or message this chapter's words exist for, then say the same thing back.
payoff.note: Wordlist derived from the A2 mock audit, as in 431-437. THE CHAPTER TEACHES ONE TEST: a word looks built, but does the rest of it survive without the piece? polideportivo loses poli- and deportivo stands; descansar loses des- and cansar stands; REIR LOSES re- AND NOTHING IS LEFT, which proves it was never a prefix -- the whole word is Latin ridere. That is the mirror of 434's bateria, which wears an ENDING it never earned; this chapter supplies the word that wears a PREFIX it never had. natacion adds a DOUBLET: natare arrived twice, worn down into nadar by a thousand years of mouths and lifted off the page intact as natacion, and the learned twin is the one on the timetable. torcerse reuses ES-GRAMMAR-STEM-O-UE-06 from dormir rather than re-teaching the o->ue break.
